tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.

XcodeBuildMCP provides comprehensive tooling for Apple platform development (iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS).

Only simulator workflow tools are enabled by default. If capabilities like device, macOS, debugging, or UI automation are not available, the user must configure XcodeBuildMCP to enable them. See https://xcodebuildmcp.com/docs/configuration for workflow configuration.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq/.claude/skills/alloq-implementation

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

152	    async def _reload(self, offer_id: int) -> None:
153	        async with get_asyncdb_session() as session:
154	            workspace = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
155	            if workspace is None:
156	                return
157	            view = build_view(await snapshot_map(session, workspace))
158	            self.revision = workspace.map_revision
159	        self.columns = view["columns"]
160	        self.rows = view["rows"]
161	        self.stories = view["stories"]
162	        self.task_options = view["task_options"]
163	        self.slice_options = view["slice_options"]
164	        self.story_count = view["story_count"]
165	        self.task_groups = view["task_groups"]
166	        self.archived = view["archived"]
167	        kept = {str(story["id"]) for story in self.archived}
168	        self.restore_tasks = {k: v for k, v in self.restore_tasks.items() if k in kept}
169	        if self.selected_id not in self.stories:
170	            self.selected_id = ""

172	    async def _apply(self, edit: Edit) -> Any | None:
173	        """Run one edit; a toast comes back when it did not go through."""
174	        offer_id = await open_offer_id(self)
175	        if not offer_id:
176	            return None
177	        editor = MapEditor(get_asyncdb_session, offer_id, await current_user_name(self))
178	        try:
179	            await edit(editor)
180	        except MapConflictError as exc:
181	            await self._reload(offer_id)
182	            return rx.toast.warning(str(exc), position="top-right")
183	        except MapEditError as exc:
184	            return rx.toast.error(str(exc), position="top-right")
185	        except Exception:
186	            logger.exception("Editing the map of offer %s failed", offer_id)
187	            return rx.toast.error(SAVE_ERROR, position="top-right")
188	        await self._reload(offer_id)
189	        return None

277	    async def _insert(self, kind: str, title: str, index: int | None) -> Any | None:
278	        """Add an activity or slice at ``index``; a done insert closes the popup."""
279	        add = MapEditor.add_activity if kind == INSERT_ACTIVITY else MapEditor.add_slice
280	        event = await self._apply(lambda e: add(e, self.revision, title, index))
281	        if event is None:
282	            self.insert_at = ""
283	        return event

285	    @rx.event
286	    @requires_offer_editor
287	    async def submit_insert(self, form: dict[str, Any]) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
288	        """Popup on a grid edge: kind and position come from ``insert_at``.
289	
290	        The form sends only the name, because Reflex moves a form's submit
291	        handler out of the ``rx.foreach`` that renders the edge.
292	        """
293	        kind, _, index = self.insert_at.partition(":")
294	        if kind not in (INSERT_ACTIVITY, INSERT_SLICE) or not index.isdigit():
295	            return
296	        if event := await self._insert(kind, str(form.get("title", "")), int(index)):
297	            yield event

361	    @rx.event
362	    @requires_offer_editor
363	    async def add_story(self, form: dict[str, Any]) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
364	        """Quick add in a map cell; task and slice come as hidden form fields.
365	
366	        Reflex moves a form's submit handler out of the ``rx.foreach`` that
367	        renders the cell, so the cell's ids travel in the form, not the call.
368	        """
369	        task_id = str(form.get("task_id", ""))
370	        slice_id = str(form.get("slice_id", ""))
371	        if not task_id.isdigit() or not int(task_id) or not slice_id.isdigit():
372	            yield rx.toast.error(NO_TASK, position="top-right")
373	            return
374	        title = str(form.get("title", ""))
375	        target = int(slice_id) or None
376	        if event := await self._apply(
377	            lambda e: e.add_story(self.revision, int(task_id), target, title)
378	        ):
379	            yield event

381	    @rx.event
382	    @requires_offer_editor
383	    async def save_story(self, form: dict[str, Any]) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
384	        """Save the inspector form of the selected story."""
385	        if not self.has_selection:
386	            return
387	        story_id = int(self.selected_id)
388	        # Title and story parts wrap in the inspector but stay one line.
389	        fields = {
390	            name: str(value) if name == "description" else " ".join(str(value).split())
391	            for name, value in form.items()
392	        }
393	        before = self.revision
394	        if event := await self._apply(
395	            lambda e: e.update_story(self.revision, story_id, fields)
396	        ):
397	            yield event
398	        elif self.revision != before:
399	            yield rx.toast.success(SAVED, position="top-right")

401	    @rx.event
402	    @requires_offer_editor
403	    async def apply_list_changes(
404	        self, changes: list[dict[str, Any]]
405	    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
406	        """Save cells edited in the list; keys are ``<story id>|<column>``."""
407	        fields: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
408	        rejected = 0
409	        for change in changes:
410	            story_id, _, column = str(change.get("key", "")).partition("|")
411	            value = str(change.get("value", ""))
412	            if column not in LIST_COLUMNS:
413	                continue
414	            if story_id not in self.stories:
415	                rejected += 1
416	                continue
417	            if column == "story":
418	                parts = parse_story_sentence(value)
419	                if parts is None:
420	                    rejected += 1
421	                    continue
422	                update = dict(zip(("role", "goal", "benefit"), parts, strict=True))
423	            else:
424	                update = {column: value}
425	            fields.setdefault(int(story_id), {}).update(update)
426	        if fields and (
427	            event := await self._apply(
428	                lambda e: e.update_stories(self.revision, fields)
429	            )
430	        ):
431	            yield event
432	        if rejected:
433	            yield _rejected_toast(rejected)

470	    @requires_offer_editor
471	    async def restore_story(self, story_id: int) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
472	        """Bring an archived story back under its chosen live task."""
473	        row = next((r for r in self.archived_rows if r["id"] == story_id), None)
474	        if row is None:
475	            return
476	        if not row["task"]:
477	            yield rx.toast.error(PICK_TASK, position="top-right")
478	            return
479	        task_id = int(row["task"])
480	        if event := await self._apply(
481	            lambda e: e.unarchive_story(self.revision, story_id, task_id)
482	        ):
483	            yield event
484	        else:

# Story map

This page lists all 126 user stories of Alloq on one map. The stories come from the code at v2.0.4, plus the offers that are not yet released. Each story lives on a feature page, and the map links to it. The map shows titles only. The acceptance criteria and the evidence are on the feature pages.

## Vision and goals

Alloq helps a software team plan which people work on which project in each week. It counts the free capacity of each person after absences, public holidays, part time and internal work, and it shows the state of the project portfolio. It also keeps the offers that the company sends to customers.

Alloq has five personas. Their goals come from the README and from the "so that" part of the stories.

**Administrator.**

- Decide who can sign in and what each person may read or change.
- Keep the roles, daily rates, departments and public holidays that the planning and the prices use.
- Give desktop users access to the central database.

**Project manager.**

- Plan people on projects week by week without overbooking anyone.
- Keep the data, status and risks of each project current.
- See the schedule, budget, risks and staffing gaps of the portfolio on one page.

**Employee.**

from alloq_commons.components.excel_grid import column_resize, resize_handle
from alloq_commons.components.toolbar import segmented, toolbar_search
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_offer.workshop.components.archive_dialog import (
    archive_button,
    archive_dialog,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.components.map_list import story_list
from alloq_offer.workshop.components.map_proposal import (
    map_proposal,
    map_proposal_panel,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.map_state import (
    INSERT_ACTIVITY,
    INSERT_SLICE,
    VIEW_LIST,
    VIEWS,
    MapState,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.workshop_state import WorkshopState

SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER = "Stories suchen"
SLICE_PLACEHOLDER = "Umsetzungsschnitte"
SKELETON_ONLY = "Nur Skeleton"
RESET_FILTERS = "Filter zurücksetzen"
NAME_PLACEHOLDER = "Name"
OK = "OK"
CANCEL = "Abbrechen"
ADD_ACTIVITY = "Aktivität hinzufügen"
ADD_SLICE = "Umsetzungsschnitt hinzufügen"
ADD_STORY = "Story hinzufügen"
SKELETON = "Skeleton"
DELETE_SLICE = "Umsetzungsschnitt löschen"
DELETE_SLICE_HINT = "Schnitt löschen – die Stories bleiben ohne Schnitt erhalten"
TOGGLE_SLICE = "Schnitt ein- oder ausklappen"
COLUMN_LINE = "1px solid var(--alloq-border-strong)"
"""Activity column lines; as strong as the month lines of the planning grid."""
COLUMN_WIDTHS_KEY = "aq-map-columns-"
"""Prefix of the localStorage key for this viewer's column widths per offer."""

Row = ObjectVar[dict[str, Any]]


def _story_card(story: Row) -> rx.Component:
    """Light blue card; hover and the selected story are styled in aq-workshop.css."""
    return rx.el.button(
        mn.stack(
            mn.group(
                mn.text(story["key"], fz="xs", c=theme.TEXT_MUTED, style=theme.NUMERIC),
                rx.cond(
                    story["skeleton"],
                    mn.badge(SKELETON, variant="outline", size="xs"),
                ),
                justify="space-between",
                wrap="nowrap",
            ),
            mn.text(story["title"], fw=600, fz="xs"),
            gap=2,
        ),
        type="button",
        on_click=MapState.select_story(story["id"]),
        custom_attrs={"data-selected": MapState.selected_id == story["id"].to_string()},
        class_name="aq-story-card",
    )


def _cell(cell: Row, slice_id: rx.Var) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.stack(
        rx.foreach(cell["stories"].to(list[dict[str, Any]]), _story_card),
        _add_story_form(cell, slice_id),
        gap=8,
        p=10,
        style={"borderLeft": COLUMN_LINE},
    )


def _add_story_form(cell: Row, slice_id: rx.Var) -> rx.Component:
    """Quick add at the bottom of a cell: type a title, Enter or the plus adds it.

    The cell's ids are hidden fields; the submit handler cannot read loop vars.
    """
    return rx.form(
        rx.el.input(type="hidden", name="task_id", value=cell["task_id"].to_string()),
        rx.el.input(type="hidden", name="slice_id", value=slice_id.to_string()),
        mn.text_input(
            name="title",
            placeholder=ADD_STORY,
            size="xs",
            right_section=mn.action_icon(
                rx.icon("plus", size=14),
                type="submit",
                variant="subtle",
                color="gray",
                size="sm",
                aria_label=ADD_STORY,
            ),
            right_section_pointer_events="all",
            custom_attrs={"maxLength": 300, "aria-label": ADD_STORY},
        ),
        on_submit=MapState.add_story,
        reset_on_submit=True,
        class_name="aq-add-story",
    )


def _band(row: Row, collapsed: rx.Var[bool]) -> rx.Component:
    """Full-width slice row like a planning block header; its left part stays put."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.group(
            _insert_edge("slice", row["index"].to(int), "aq-map-plus-inline"),
            mn.action_icon(
                rx.cond(
                    collapsed,
                    rx.icon("chevron-right", size=16, stroke_width=2),
                    rx.icon("chevron-down", size=16, stroke_width=2),
                ),
                variant="subtle",
                color="gray",
                size="sm",
                on_click=MapState.toggle_slice(row["slice_id"]),
                aria_label=TOGGLE_SLICE,
            ),
            rx.cond(
                row["editable"],
                mn.text_input(
                    default_value=row["title"],
                    key=row["title"].to(str),
                    on_blur=lambda value: MapState.rename_slice(row["slice_id"], value),  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
                    size="xs",
                    variant="unstyled",
                    custom_attrs={
                        "maxLength": 255,
                        "aria-label": "Name des Schnitts",
                        "title": row["title"],
                    },
                    class_name="aq-map-title",
                    w=280,
                ),
                mn.text(row["title"], fw=600, fz="13px", c=theme.TEXT_MUTED),
            ),
            mn.text(row["count_label"].to(str), fz="12px", c=theme.TEXT_MUTED),
            gap=6,
            wrap="nowrap",
            align="center",
            class_name="aq-band-pin",
        ),
        rx.cond(
            row["editable"],
            mn.box(
                mn.tooltip(
                    mn.action_icon(
                        rx.icon("x", size=14),
                        variant="subtle",
                        color="red",
                        size="sm",
                        on_click=MapState.delete_slice(row["slice_id"]),
                        aria_label=DELETE_SLICE,
                    ),
                    label=DELETE_SLICE_HINT,
                    with_arrow=True,
                    z_index=theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX,
                ),
                class_name="aq-band-end",
            ),
        ),
        class_name="aq-map-band",
    )


def _row(row: Row) -> rx.Component:
    collapsed = MapState.collapsed_slices.contains(row["slice_id"].to_string())
    return rx.fragment(
        _band(row, collapsed),
        rx.cond(
            collapsed,
            rx.fragment(),
            rx.box(
                rx.foreach(
                    row["cells"].to(list[dict[str, Any]]),
                    lambda cell: _cell(cell, row["slice_id"]),
                ),
                display="grid",
                grid_template_columns=MapState.grid_template,
                class_name="aq-map-row",
            ),
        ),
    )


def _column_title(column: Row) -> rx.Component:
    """Title shown on at most two lines; the text area over it edits it."""
    return mn.box(
        mn.text(column["title"], fz="xs", fw=600, lh="1.4", class_name="aq-clamp-view"),
        mn.textarea(
            default_value=column["title"],
            key=column["title"].to(str),
            on_blur=lambda value: MapState.rename_activity(column["id"], value),  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
            variant="unstyled",
            custom_attrs={
                "maxLength": 255,
                "aria-label": "Name der Aktivität",
                "title": column["title"],
            },
            class_name="aq-clamp-input",
        ),
        class_name="aq-clamp-edit",
    )


def _column(column: Row) -> rx.Component:
    """Activity header: editable title with its move and archive icons on the right."""
    return mn.group(
        _column_title(column),
        mn.group(
            mn.tooltip(
                mn.action_icon(
                    rx.icon("chevron-left", size=14),
                    variant="subtle",
                    color="gray",
                    size="sm",
                    disabled=column["first"],
                    on_click=MapState.move_activity(column["id"], -1),
                    aria_label="Nach links",
                ),
                label="Aktivität nach links verschieben",
                with_arrow=True,
                z_index=theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX,
            ),
            mn.tooltip(
                mn.action_icon(
                    rx.icon("chevron-right", size=14),
                    variant="subtle",
                    color="gray",
                    size="sm",
                    disabled=column["last"],
                    on_click=MapState.move_activity(column["id"], 1),
                    aria_label="Nach rechts",
                ),
                label="Aktivität nach rechts verschieben",
                with_arrow=True,
                z_index=theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX,
            ),
            mn.tooltip(
                mn.action_icon(
                    rx.icon("x", size=14),
                    variant="subtle",
                    color="red",
                    size="sm",
                    on_click=MapState.archive_activity(column["id"]),
                    aria_label="Aktivität archivieren",
                ),
                label="Aktivität archivieren (nur ohne Stories)",
                with_arrow=True,
                z_index=theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX,
            ),
            gap=0,
            wrap="nowrap",
        ),
        rx.cond(column["first"], _insert_edge("activity", 0, "aq-map-plus-xl")),
        _insert_edge("activity", column["index"].to(int) + 1, "aq-map-plus-x"),
        resize_handle(column["id"]),
        gap=4,
        wrap="nowrap",
        align="flex-start",
        p=10,
        pos="relative",
        style={"borderLeft": COLUMN_LINE},
    )


INSERT_TITLES = {INSERT_ACTIVITY: ADD_ACTIVITY, INSERT_SLICE: ADD_SLICE}


def _insert_edge(kind: str, index: rx.Var[int] | int, edge: str) -> rx.Component:
    """Plus on a grid edge; its popup names the activity or slice to insert."""
    title = INSERT_TITLES[kind]
    key = f"{kind}:" + rx.Var.create(index).to_string()
    return mn.popover(
        mn.popover.target(
            mn.action_icon(
                rx.icon("plus", size=12),
                variant="default",
                radius="xl",
                size=18,
                on_click=MapState.open_insert(key),
                aria_label=title,
                class_name=f"aq-map-plus {edge}",
            ),
        ),
        mn.popover.dropdown(
            rx.form(
                mn.stack(
                    mn.text(title, fz="13px", fw=650),
                    mn.text_input(
                        name="title",
                        placeholder=NAME_PLACEHOLDER,
                        size="xs",
                        data_autofocus=True,
                        custom_attrs={"maxLength": 255, "aria-label": title},
                    ),
                    mn.group(
                        mn.button(
                            CANCEL,
                            type="button",
                            variant="default",
                            size="xs",
                            on_click=MapState.close_insert,
                        ),
                        mn.button(OK, type="submit", size="xs"),
                        justify="flex-end",
                        gap=6,
                    ),
                    gap=8,
                ),
                # Only the name: the loop variable behind ``index`` does not
                # exist in the submit handler Reflex builds for the form.
                on_submit=MapState.submit_insert,
                reset_on_submit=True,
            ),
        ),
        opened=MapState.insert_at == key,
        on_close=MapState.close_insert,
        position="bottom",
        with_arrow=True,
        trap_focus=True,
        shadow="md",
        width=260,
        z_index=theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX,
    )


def _grid() -> rx.Component:
    return column_resize(
        rx.box(
            rx.box(
                rx.foreach(MapState.columns, _column),
                display="grid",
                grid_template_columns=MapState.grid_template,
                class_name="aq-map-head",
            ),
            rx.foreach(MapState.visible_rows, _row),
            class_name="aq-map-grid",
        ),
        REDACTED + WorkshopState.offer_id.to_string(),
        class_name="aq-map-scroll",
    )


def _footer() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.group(
        mn.box(map_proposal(), ml="auto"),
        gap=12,
        class_name="aq-map-footer",
    )


def _filter_select(
    data: rx.Var | list[str],
    value: rx.Var[list[str]],
    on_change: rx.event.EventType[list[str]],
    placeholder: str,
    label: rx.Var[str],
) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.multi_select(
        data=data,
        value=value,
        on_change=on_change,
        placeholder=placeholder,
        clearable=True,
        size="xs",
        w="11rem",
        class_name=rx.cond(
            value.length() > 0, "alloq-filter-ms has-mehr", "alloq-filter-ms"
        ),
        style={"--alloq-mehr": label},
    )


def map_filter_row() -> rx.Component:
    """Filter bar of the map: view, story search, slices and skeleton filter."""
    return mn.group(
        segmented(MapState.view, MapState.set_view, VIEWS),
        toolbar_search(
            MapState.map_search, MapState.set_map_search, SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER
        ),
        _filter_select(
            MapState.slice_options,
            MapState.slice_filter,
            MapState.set_slice_filter,
            SLICE_PLACEHOLDER,
            MapState.slice_filter_label,
        ),
        mn.switch(
            label=SKELETON_ONLY,
            checked=MapState.skeleton_only,
            on_change=MapState.set_skeleton_only,
            color="blue",
            size="xs",
        ),
        rx.cond(
            MapState.is_filtered,
            mn.button(
                RESET_FILTERS,
                variant="subtle",
                color="gray",
                size="compact-xs",
                on_click=MapState.reset_filters,
            ),
        ),
        mn.group(
            archive_button(),
            mn.text(MapState.summary, fz="12px", c=theme.TEXT_MUTED),
            gap=8,
            ml="auto",
        ),
        gap=8,
        w="100%",
    )


def map_section() -> rx.Component:
    """Map grid or story list filling the pane, the open proposal and the footer."""
    return rx.fragment(
        rx.cond(MapState.view == VIEW_LIST, story_list(), _grid()),
        map_proposal_panel(),
        _footer(),
        archive_dialog(),
    )

"""The story map as a list: one line per story, edited like a spreadsheet."""

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons import theme
from alloq_commons.components.excel_grid import (
    column_width,
    excel_grid,
    grid_cell_attrs,
    grid_row_attrs,
    resize_handle,
)
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.map_state import MapState
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.workshop_state import WorkshopState

LIST_LABEL = "Story-Liste"
DETAILS = "Details öffnen"
LIST_COLUMNS = (
    ("activity", "Aktivität", 180, 0),
    ("title", "Story", 240, 300),
    ("story", "User Story", 420, 1000),
    ("description", "Beschreibung", 320, 4000),
)
"""Column key, header, default width in px and text limit (0: read only)."""
DETAILS_WIDTH = "44px"
COLUMN_WIDTHS_KEY = "aq-story-list-columns-"
"""Prefix of the localStorage key for this viewer's column widths per offer."""
_TRACKS = [column_width(key, width) for key, _, width, _ in LIST_COLUMNS]
# The last text column also takes the space left over.
TEMPLATE = " ".join([*_TRACKS[:-1], f"minmax({_TRACKS[-1]}, 1fr)", DETAILS_WIDTH])

Row = ObjectVar[dict[str, Any]]


def _cell(row: Row, column: str, limit: int) -> rx.Component:
    value = row[column].to(str)
    attrs = grid_cell_attrs(row["id"].to_string() + "|" + column, column, value)
    attrs.update(
        {
            "data-cell-type": "text",
            "data-read-only": "false" if limit else "true",
            "data-max-length": limit or 255,
            "title": value,
        }
    )
    return mn.box(
        value,
        custom_attrs=attrs,
        class_name="aq-list-cell",
        c=theme.TEXT if limit else theme.TEXT_MUTED,
    )


def _row(row: Row) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        *(_cell(row, column, limit) for column, _, _, limit in LIST_COLUMNS),
        mn.box(
            mn.action_icon(
                rx.icon("panel-right-open", size=15),
                variant="subtle",
                color="gray",
                size="sm",
                on_click=MapState.select_story(row["id"]),
                aria_label=DETAILS,
                custom_attrs={"title": DETAILS},
            ),
            class_name="aq-list-details",
        ),
        custom_attrs={
            **grid_row_attrs(row["id"].to_string(), "stories"),
            "data-selected": MapState.selected_id == row["id"].to_string(),
        },
        class_name="aq-list-row",
        style={"gridTemplateColumns": TEMPLATE},
    )


def _header() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        *(
            mn.box(title, resize_handle(key), class_name="aq-list-head-cell")
            for key, title, _, _ in LIST_COLUMNS
        ),
        mn.box(class_name="aq-list-head-cell"),
        class_name="aq-list-head",
        custom_attrs={"data-grid-header": "true"},
        style={"gridTemplateColumns": TEMPLATE},
    )


def story_list() -> rx.Component:
    """Stories of the visible rows; title, sentence and description are editable."""
    return excel_grid(
        _header(),
        rx.foreach(MapState.list_rows, _row),
        id="story-list-grid",
        grid_label=LIST_LABEL,
        revision=MapState.revision,
        dirty=False,
        saving=False,
        navigation_guard=False,
        resize_key=COLUMN_WIDTHS_KEY + WorkshopState.offer_id.to_string(),
        on_commit=MapState.apply_list_changes,
        on_reject=MapState.notify_rejected,
        class_name="aq-map-scroll aq-story-list",
        style={"outline": "none"},
    )

"""Turn a proposed map and briefing into stored rows and a map revision."""

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.schemas import (
    ProposedBriefing,
    ProposedMap,
    ProposedStory,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    ActivityEntity,
    MapRevisionEntity,
    Origin,
    SliceEntity,
    StatementEntity,
    StatementType,
    StoryEntity,
    TaskEntity,
    WorkspaceEntity,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.chapters import mark_dependent_review
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.story_rules import story_problems, story_sentence

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

KEY_PREFIX = "US-"
EVIDENCE_TYPES = (StatementType.REQUIREMENT, StatementType.FACT)


@dataclass
class ApplyResult:
    stories: int = 0
    statements: int = 0
    skipped: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def next_story_key(workspace: WorkspaceEntity) -> str:
    """The next story key; the counter only grows, so keys are never reused."""
    workspace.story_seq += 1
    return f"{KEY_PREFIX}{workspace.story_seq:02d}"


def _known_refs(refs: list[int], valid_block_ids: set[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Refs that point at a real block; invented ones are dropped."""
    kept = [ref for ref in dict.fromkeys(refs) if ref in valid_block_ids]
    if len(kept) < len(set(refs)):
        logger.warning("Dropped %d unknown source refs", len(set(refs)) - len(kept))
    return kept


def new_story(
    workspace: WorkspaceEntity,
    story: ProposedStory,
    *,
    task_id: int,
    slice_id: int | None,
    position: int,
    valid_block_ids: set[int],
) -> StoryEntity:
    """A stored story from a proposal: app key and checked origin."""
    refs = _known_refs(story.source_refs, valid_block_ids)
    return StoryEntity(
        offer_id=workspace.offer_id,
        key=next_story_key(workspace),
        title=story.title.strip(),
        role=story.role.strip(),
        goal=story.goal.strip(),
        benefit=story.benefit.strip(),
        # Without a surviving source ref the wish is not verifiable.
        origin=(
            Origin.CUSTOMER
            if story.origin == Origin.CUSTOMER and refs
            else Origin.PROPOSAL
        ),
        task_id=task_id,
        slice_id=slice_id,
        skeleton=story.skeleton,
        position=position,
        source_refs=refs,
    )


async def apply_proposed_map(
    session: AsyncSession,
    workspace: WorkspaceEntity,
    proposed: ProposedMap,
    valid_block_ids: set[int],
) -> ApplyResult:
    """Store an initial map. The app assigns the keys; the model never does."""
    result = ApplyResult()
    offer_id = workspace.offer_id
    if proposed.vision and not workspace.vision:
        workspace.vision = proposed.vision
    if proposed.roles and not workspace.roles:
        workspace.roles = list(dict.fromkeys(proposed.roles))

    slices: dict[str, SliceEntity] = {}
    for position, title in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(proposed.slices), 1):
        slices[title] = SliceEntity(offer_id=offer_id, title=title, position=position)
        session.add(slices[title])
    await session.flush()

    story_position = 0
    for a_pos, activity in enumerate(proposed.activities, 1):
        activity_row = ActivityEntity(
            offer_id=offer_id, title=activity.title, position=a_pos
        )
        session.add(activity_row)
        await session.flush()
        for t_pos, task in enumerate(activity.tasks, 1):

def next_story_key(workspace: WorkspaceEntity) -> str:
    """The next story key; the counter only grows, so keys are never reused."""
    workspace.story_seq += 1
    return f"{KEY_PREFIX}{workspace.story_seq:02d}"


def _known_refs(refs: list[int], valid_block_ids: set[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Refs that point at a real block; invented ones are dropped."""
    kept = [ref for ref in dict.fromkeys(refs) if ref in valid_block_ids]
    if len(kept) < len(set(refs)):
        logger.warning("Dropped %d unknown source refs", len(set(refs)) - len(kept))
    return kept

    workspace: WorkspaceEntity,

    task_id: int,

            else Origin.PROPOSAL
        ),
        task_id=task_id,
        slice_id=slice_id,

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from sqlalchemy import func, select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    ActivityEntity,
    MapRevisionEntity,

    StoryEntity,
    TaskEntity,

)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import workspace_repo
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.chapters import mark_dependent_review
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.map_apply import next_story_key, snapshot_map
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.story_rules import (
    MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH,
    STORY_FIELDS,
    story_problems,
)

CONFLICT = (
    "Die Map wurde inzwischen geändert. Die aktuelle Fassung wurde geladen, "
    "bitte wiederholen Sie die Änderung."
)
NOT_FOUND = "Das Element gibt es nicht mehr."
NOT_ARCHIVED = "Die Story ist nicht archiviert."
ACTIVITY_NOT_EMPTY = "Die Aktivität enthält noch Stories. Archivieren Sie diese zuerst."
DEFAULT_TASK = "Hauptaufgabe"
BLANK_TITLE = "Bitte geben Sie einen Namen ein."
DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG = "Die Beschreibung ist zu lang."
NEW_STORY_TITLE = "Neue Story"


class MapConflictError(RuntimeError):
    """Someone else changed the map since the editor loaded it (A08)."""


class MapEditError(ValueError):
    """The edit is not allowed; the message is German and shown to users."""


@asynccontextmanager
async def map_edit(
    session_factory: SessionFactory, offer_id: int, expected_revision: int
) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[AsyncSession, WorkspaceEntity]]:
    """A transaction on the locked workspace; a stale ``expected_revision`` fails."""
    async with session_factory() as session:
        workspace = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
        if workspace is None:
            raise MapEditError(NOT_FOUND)
        await session.refresh(workspace, with_for_update=True)
        if workspace.map_revision != expected_revision:
            raise MapConflictError(CONFLICT)
        yield session, workspace


async def record(session: AsyncSession, workspace: WorkspaceEntity, user: str) -> int:
    """Bump the revision and keep an immutable snapshot of the result."""
    await session.flush()
    workspace.map_revision += 1
    await mark_dependent_review(session, workspace)
    session.add(
        MapRevisionEntity(
            offer_id=workspace.offer_id,
            revision=workspace.map_revision,
            snapshot=await snapshot_map(session, workspace),
            created_by=user,
        )
    )
    return workspace.map_revision


def _title(value: str) -> str:
    title = value.strip()
    if not title:
        raise MapEditError(BLANK_TITLE)
    return title[:255]


async def _own[T: ActivityEntity | TaskEntity | StoryEntity | SliceEntity](
    session: AsyncSession, entity: type[T], offer_id: int, row_id: int
) -> T:
    row = await session.get(entity, row_id)
    if (
        row is None
        or row.offer_id != offer_id
        or getattr(row, "archived_at", None) is not None
    ):
        raise MapEditError(NOT_FOUND)
    return row


async def _next_position(
    session: AsyncSession,
    entity: type[ActivityEntity | TaskEntity | SliceEntity | StoryEntity],
    *where: object,
) -> int:
    highest = await session.scalar(select(func.max(entity.position)).where(*where))  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
    return (highest or 0) + 1


async def _insert[T: ActivityEntity | SliceEntity](
    session: AsyncSession, row: T, index: int | None, *where: object
) -> T:
    """Add ``row`` at ``index`` among the rows matching ``where`` (end when None)."""
    entity = type(row)
    rows = list(
        (
            await session.scalars(
                select(entity).where(*where).order_by(entity.position, entity.id)  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
            )
        ).all()
    )
    rows.insert(len(rows) if index is None else max(index, 0), row)
    for position, item in enumerate(rows, 1):
        item.position = position
    session.add(row)
    await session.flush()
    return row


def _apply_story_text(story: StoryEntity, fields: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
    """Set title, role, goal, benefit and description; True when one changed."""
    values = {
        name: fields.get(name, getattr(story, name)).strip()
        for name in (*STORY_FIELDS, "description")
    }
    problems = story_problems(*(values[name] for name in STORY_FIELDS))
    if len(values["description"]) > MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH:
        problems.append(DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG)
    if problems:
        raise MapEditError(" ".join(problems))

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from sqlalchemy import func, select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    ActivityEntity,
    MapRevisionEntity,
    Origin,
    SliceEntity,
    StoryEntity,
    TaskEntity,
    WorkspaceEntity,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import workspace_repo
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.chapters import mark_dependent_review
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.map_apply import next_story_key, snapshot_map
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.story_rules import (
    MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH,
    STORY_FIELDS,
    story_problems,
)

CONFLICT = (
    "Die Map wurde inzwischen geändert. Die aktuelle Fassung wurde geladen, "
    "bitte wiederholen Sie die Änderung."
)
NOT_FOUND = "Das Element gibt es nicht mehr."
NOT_ARCHIVED = "Die Story ist nicht archiviert."
ACTIVITY_NOT_EMPTY = "Die Aktivität enthält noch Stories. Archivieren Sie diese zuerst."
DEFAULT_TASK = "Hauptaufgabe"
BLANK_TITLE = "Bitte geben Sie einen Namen ein."
DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG = "Die Beschreibung ist zu lang."
NEW_STORY_TITLE = "Neue Story"


class MapConflictError(RuntimeError):
    """Someone else changed the map since the editor loaded it (A08)."""


class MapEditError(ValueError):
    """The edit is not allowed; the message is German and shown to users."""


@asynccontextmanager
async def map_edit(
    session_factory: SessionFactory, offer_id: int, expected_revision: int
) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[AsyncSession, WorkspaceEntity]]:
    """A transaction on the locked workspace; a stale ``expected_revision`` fails."""
    async with session_factory() as session:
        workspace = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
        if workspace is None:
            raise MapEditError(NOT_FOUND)
        await session.refresh(workspace, with_for_update=True)
        if workspace.map_revision != expected_revision:
            raise MapConflictError(CONFLICT)
        yield session, workspace


async def record(session: AsyncSession, workspace: WorkspaceEntity, user: str) -> int:
    """Bump the revision and keep an immutable snapshot of the result."""
    await session.flush()
    workspace.map_revision += 1
    await mark_dependent_review(session, workspace)
    session.add(
        MapRevisionEntity(
            offer_id=workspace.offer_id,
            revision=workspace.map_revision,
            snapshot=await snapshot_map(session, workspace),
            created_by=user,
        )
    )
    return workspace.map_revision


def _title(value: str) -> str:
    title = value.strip()
    if not title:
        raise MapEditError(BLANK_TITLE)
    return title[:255]


async def _own[T: ActivityEntity | TaskEntity | StoryEntity | SliceEntity](
    session: AsyncSession, entity: type[T], offer_id: int, row_id: int
) -> T:
    row = await session.get(entity, row_id)
    if (
        row is None
        or row.offer_id != offer_id
        or getattr(row, "archived_at", None) is not None
    ):
        raise MapEditError(NOT_FOUND)
    return row


async def _next_position(
    session: AsyncSession,
    entity: type[ActivityEntity | TaskEntity | SliceEntity | StoryEntity],
    *where: object,
) -> int:
    highest = await session.scalar(select(func.max(entity.position)).where(*where))  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
    return (highest or 0) + 1


async def _insert[T: ActivityEntity | SliceEntity](
    session: AsyncSession, row: T, index: int | None, *where: object
) -> T:
    """Add ``row`` at ``index`` among the rows matching ``where`` (end when None)."""
    entity = type(row)
    rows = list(
        (
            await session.scalars(
                select(entity).where(*where).order_by(entity.position, entity.id)  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
            )
        ).all()
    )
    rows.insert(len(rows) if index is None else max(index, 0), row)
    for position, item in enumerate(rows, 1):
        item.position = position
    session.add(row)
    await session.flush()
    return row


def _apply_story_text(story: StoryEntity, fields: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
    """Set title, role, goal, benefit and description; True when one changed."""
    values = {

    if len(values["description"]) > MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH:
        problems.append(DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG)
    if problems:
        raise MapEditError(" ".join(problems))
